newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Davomas says in 40,000 tonnes cocoa deal.
newsitem.headline: Davomas says in 40,000 tonnes cocoa deal.

text.p: Indonesia's largest cocoa producer PT Davomas Abadi said on Thursday it had secured a 10-year contract to sell 40,000 tonnes of cocoa powder and butter per year to a foreign firm.
"We have recently signed a deal to supply 40,000 tonnes of cocoa powder and cocoa butter annually for a period of 10 years," Davomas senior official Bob Boetar Boetar told Reuters.
Boetar Boetar declined to elaborate on the value of the contract and the buyer, but said prices would be set on market prices on time of delivery.
He said cocoa butter was currently traded between 8,500 rupiah to 8,700 rupiah per kg, while cocoa powder was between 1,200 rupiah to 1,400 rupiah per kg.
"This is a significant deal for us, as supplying 40,000 tonnes means using two production lines. We have currently only three production lines each producing 20,000 tonnes," Boetar Boetar said.
He said he expected the first delivery to take place in January 1998.
He said the company planned to boost production capacity to 160,000 tonnes by the year 1999 in line with expected rising demand.
Davomas also expected to diversify into downstream products including chocolate production because of Indonesia's huge population of 200 million people and a low chocolate consumption rate, he said.
